case.question: I fish for salmon from a boat. For this week, how good do you expect boat fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Muskegon or Grand Haven by boat.** I'd rate both a 3 (good) for this week.
- **Muskegon:** fish 120-200 ft of water, with lines at about 35-90 ft down. Green and blue spoons, plus white flies, were the producers.
- **Grand Haven:** fish 130-240 ft of water, with lines at about 30-120 ft down. Use spoons.
- **St. Joseph:** I'd rate it 2 overall. It's good if you're after coho (3) from 40+ ft on spoons, but Chinook were only below average (1).
- **South Haven:** I'd rate it 2 (average). Fish were spread out, so expect to cover water.
- **Caveat:** the latest reports are from May 18, so check the forecast before you go. Gusts reached 36-41 mph that week.

## Why

- Muskegon and Grand Haven boats both had good salmon fishing in the latest reports, while South Haven was only fair (Muskegon, 2022-05-18; Grand Haven, 2022-05-18; South Haven, 2022-05-18).
- St. Joseph's good boat result was for coho, not Chinook, so I'd expect the Chinook odds there to be lower (St. Joseph, 2022-05-18).
- I'd expect Muskegon to be a slightly better bet than Grand Haven because its report gave the most specific lure and depth guidance, though the two are close.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (latest is May 18, six days old)**
- Muskegon, 2022-05-18: "Boats were doing well catching salmon 35 to 90 feet down in 120 to 200 feet of water. … Green and blue spoons were working well along with white flies. … A few salmon were caught on meat rigs." Quality 3.
- Grand Haven, 2022-05-18: "The salmon action was good 30 to 120 feet down in 130 to 240 feet of water." Quality 3.
- St. Joseph, 2022-05-18: "Boat anglers targeting salmon had good fishing… Catches were mostly coho and steelhead." Coho from boats: quality 3. Chinook from boats: quality 1, "a few Chinook and lake trout mixed in."
- South Haven, 2022-05-18: "Boat anglers targeting salmon had fair fishing. … The fish were spread out from 30 feet of water to deeper depths. … Most boats were trolling spoons." Quality 2.
- Pier fishing was slow at all four ports that week (quality 1 at most), so boats are the better choice.

**Past seasons (similar water temperature)**
- The similar-water search (about 53 F, within 21 days of today) only returned the May 18 and May 4 2022 reports, so I have no earlier-season comparison for this week.
- I'd expect the May 4 St. Joseph boat report (coho good in 30 ft, quality 3) to be less relevant now, since the fish have since moved deeper.

**Conditions now**
- Live conditions were unavailable: the conditions tool returned a summary for the week before today, not current readings.
- Buoy surface water for the week of May 18: about 52-53 F at St. Joseph and South Haven (buoy 45168) and 52 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon (buoy 45029), each up 3-5 F that week.
- Muskegon had fewer upwelling hours (14 in the last 3 days) than Grand Haven (26) or St. Joseph (18), and Grand Haven was the most upwelling-favored. I'd expect that to matter less than the fish depth already reported.

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old, and the season moves fast in May. Treat these ratings as a guide.
- The conditions figures are from the week before today, not live, so I couldn't check the current forecast or whether the fish are still at those depths.
- The ratings are my estimates from one week of reports, not DNR ratings.
- The reports don't say what lures worked for Grand Haven or St. Joseph Chinook beyond what's quoted above.

## Sources

- DNR weekly report, May 18 2022 (covers all four ports): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3186585
- DNR weekly report, May 4 2022 (St. Joseph, Grand Haven, South Haven, background only): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3166173
